items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATION

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the environmental conservation law and the state finance law,
in relation to the disposition of certain fees and penalties
items.lawCode: Amd En Con L, generally; amd §83, St Fin L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4033

SPONSOR: HARCKHAM
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the environmental conservation law and the state finance
law, in relation to the disposition of certain fees and penalties

 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the environmental conservation law and the state finance
law, in relation to the disposition of certain fees and penalties

 
PURPOSE:

Relates to the disposition of certain fees and penalties.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the environmental conservation law to establish that
fees paid for certain environmental violations will be deposited into
New York's conservation enforcement account.

Section 2 amends the finance law to establish that fees paid for certain
environmental violations will be deposited into a special account within
the conservation fund, which will be known as the conservation enforce-
ment account. All of such moneys, revenues and interest shall be avail-
able to the department of environmental conservation, pursuant to appro-
priation, exclusively for funding the enforcement of the environmental
conservation laws

Sections 3 and 4 amend the environmental conservation law to set fine
amounts for certain environmental violations.

Section 5 amends the environmental conservation law to establish that
money received by a town justice or a village justice in any action for
a penalty or a fine for a violation will be paid to the State Comp-
troller. The State Comptroller will pay all lawful fees for services
when instituted by order of the department or upon information of a
conservation officer, regional and assistant regional conservation offi-
cer, special game protector, district ranger, forest ranger, or member
of the state police. The balance of the fund will be credited to the
State Comptroller.

Section 6 through 69 set fine rates for civil, criminal, and administra-
tive charges relating to the environmental conservation law.

Section 70 states the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Violations of environmental law such as causing a fire on state lands,
or introducing invasive species can have disastrous impacts on the envi-
ronment, often costing the state and municipalities valuable time and
money to remediate the damage. Moreover, the resources needed to enforce
these laws can be costly as well.

This legislation will provide that fees paid for certain environmental
violations are deposited into New York's conservation enforcement
account, ensuring that those violating our laws are taking on the costs
of enforcing them.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2023-2024: S7086B/A8213B - Passed Senate/Died in Environmental Conserva-
tion

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
